question: Given a fixed FLOP budget, how should model size and number of training tokens be traded off for a transformer language model?
hypothesis: Model size and training tokens should be scaled in equal proportion, so current large LMs are over-sized and under-trained.
contributions: Three independent estimation approaches (training-curve envelope, IsoFLOP profiles, parametric loss fit) that agree on near-equal scaling of parameters and tokens
Chinchilla: 70B parameters, 1.4T tokens, same compute as Gopher, outperforming Gopher, GPT-3, Jurassic-1 and MT-NLG 530B
Evidence that dataset scale and quality need more focus

method.summary: Trained over 400 transformers (70M to 16B+ params, 5B to 500B tokens) on MassiveText with several cosine cycle lengths, fit power laws for optimal N and D versus FLOPs three ways, then trained Chinchilla (70B, 1.4T tokens) at Gopher's compute (5.76e23 FLOPs) and evaluated it on language modelling, MMLU, BIG-bench, reading comprehension, QA, common sense, bias and toxicity.

limits: Only two large-scale runs (Chinchilla and Gopher), no intermediate scales
Assumes a power-law frontier; observed concavity in log N_opt at high compute suggests optimal models may be even smaller
All runs under one epoch; multi-epoch regime untested
Overlap between larger training data and test sets may inflate language modelling results
Only autoregressive text models; other hyperparameters rely on heuristics
Approach 3 uncertainty interval implausibly narrow (later shown by Besiroglu et al. 2024, outside this source)
